stem: To find the distance \(AB\) across a pond, a surveyor stands at point \(C\), away from the pond, and sights both \(A\) and \(B\). She marks point \(D\) on \(\overline{CA}\) and point \(E\) on \(\overline{CB}\) so that \(\overline{DE}\) is parallel to \(\overline{AB}\), as shown. She measures \(CD = 32\) meters, \(DA = 48\) meters, and \(DE = 26\) meters. What is the distance \(AB\), in meters? Note: Figure not drawn to scale.
solution: Because \(\overline{DE}\) is parallel to \(\overline{AB}\), triangle \(CDE\) is similar to triangle \(CAB\).
verify:
P=figure['points']
d=lambda a,b: sqrt((P[a][0]-P[b][0])**2+(P[a][1]-P[b][1])**2)
ang=lambda a,v,b: N(acos(((P[a][0]-P[v][0])*(P[b][0]-P[v][0])+(P[a][1]-P[v][1])*(P[b][1]-P[v][1]))/(d(a,v)*d(b,v)))*180/pi)
assert P['D'][1]==P['E'][1] and P['A'][1]==P['B'][1] and figure['not_to_scale']
x=symbols('x')
ans=solve(Eq(x/26,Rational(32+48,32)),x)[0]
assert Rational(spr_answers[0])==ans==65
